title: About local customer optimisation within Performance Max campaign for shop goals - Google Ads Help

facts.fact: Local customer optimisation is a feature within Performance Max campaigns for shop goals that prioritises reaching potential customers who are close to or interested in the advertiser's business area and ready to take action, such as visiting or contacting.
facts.quote: Local customer optimisation is a feature within Performance Max campaigns for shop goals that allows you to prioritise reaching potential customers who are close to or interested in your business area

facts.fact: Local customer optimisation is not compatible with online campaign goals or with Performance Max campaigns that use products from Merchant Center, according to Google.
facts.quote: Local customer optimisation is not compatible with online campaign goals and Performance Max campaigns with products from Merchant Center.

facts.fact: The local customer optimisation toggle is available when a Performance Max campaign is created to optimise only to offline goals.
facts.quote: When you create a Performance Max campaign optimising only to offline goals, the local customer optimisation toggle will be available to turn on this feature

facts.fact: When creating a new shop-goals Performance Max campaign, the campaign objective is named "Local shop visits and promotions".
facts.quote: Choose your campaign objective as Local shop visits and promotions, then select Performance Max as the campaign type.

facts.fact: Conversion goals offered for shop-goals campaigns include shop visits, shop sales, contacts (Google-hosted) and directions (Google-hosted).
facts.quote: Confirm the conversion goals, such as shop visits, shop sales, contacts (Google-hosted) or directions (Google-hosted) for shop goals for your campaign.

facts.fact: Target business locations can be selected from a Business Profile account or from linked location or affiliate location assets.
facts.quote: Select your business locations to target, either from your Business Profile account or your linked location or affiliate location assets.

facts.fact: If an account is linked to a Merchant Center account, the 'Advertiser products from a Merchant Center account' option must be deselected to use local customer optimisation.
facts.quote: If your account is linked to a Merchant Center account, deselect 'Advertiser products from a Merchant Center account' as local customer optimisation is not compatible with Performance Max campaigns with products from Merchant Center.

facts.fact: An existing campaign advertising products from a Merchant Center account is not compatible with local customer optimisation, even if the toggle is turned on.
facts.quote: If the selected campaign is advertising products from a Merchant Center account, it will not be compatible with local customer optimisation even if the toggle is turned on.

facts.fact: For an existing Performance Max for shop goals campaign, the local customer optimisation setting is found in the 'Budget and bidding optimisation' section of the Settings page.
facts.quote: Go to the 'Budget and bidding optimisation' section on the 'Settings' page.

facts.fact: Google states that local customer optimisation may help businesses with physical locations increase their local visibility.
facts.quote: Local customer optimisation may help businesses with physical locations increase their local visibility

facts.fact: Local customer optimisation directs campaign budgets to locally tailored ads on Google Maps, Waze and local formats on Google Search.
facts.quote: Target users near your business area by directing campaign budgets to locally tailored ads on channels such as Google Maps, Waze and local formats on Google Search.

facts.fact: The feature is intended to reach potential customers when they are actively navigating, trip planning or searching for locations on Google Maps, Waze or Google Search for a service in a specific area.
facts.quote: This campaign feature is intended to reach potential customers at the most critical moment when they are actively navigating, trip planning or searching for locations on Google Maps, Waze or Google Search
